conventions.convention: Connections and curvatures are anti-Hermitian; I₆(R) = i tr_R(F³)/(24π²). The six-form is a formal descent polynomial, not a six-form integrated on physical four-dimensional spacetime.
The general anomaly quotient uses the explicitly supplied linear counterterm space C and boundary-primitive space N; unrestricted relative cohomology applies only when both spaces are full.

The selected model has nondynamical SU(3)×U(1) backgrounds on trivial bundles over mostly-plus Minkowski space, natural units, compact support, full counterterm and boundary spaces, and an adopted common linear one-loop descent prescription.
The item sets γ₅ = iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³ and positive chirality equal to its +1 eigenspace. Its claimed identification with Bilal's convention is disputed below.
BRST anticommutes with coordinate one-forms: s(dxᵘ∧a) = −dxᵘ∧sa. Thus sB = −d_Hη despite the positive component rule, and one-ghost evaluation satisfies Eᵖ(sCₚ) = (−1)ᵖδCₚ.
The anomaly class concerns infinitesimal local transformations only; zero local class establishes neither absence of global anomalies nor consistency of dynamical gauging.

load_bearing.statement: As an explicit source-backed one-loop input, after the regulator masses are taken to infinity this selected prescription assigns to each positive-chirality species R_i the consistent local anomaly obtained by descent from I₆(R_i,A_i) of the preceding cubic-polynomial definition.

The local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly is the class of the specified quantum background-variation cocycle in Z^{1,4}/(sC+d_HN), with precisely the model's admitted linear counterterm and boundary spaces.

For E = (3,+1), its dual E*, and the induced dual connection, I₆(E*) = −I₆(E) and Q₅(E*) = −Q₅(E). Thus any common linear descent of this conjugate pair has zero total cubic polynomial and zero total first consistent descent representative.
If a local counterterm changes an anomaly representative from a₄ to a′₄ = a₄+sC₄+d_Hr₃, then [a′₄] = [a₄] in H^{1,4}(s|d_H).

concerns.concern: The Definition sets γ₅ = iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³ = −iγ₀γ₁γ₂γ₃ and says this is “Bilal's mostly-plus positive-chirality convention, Eq. (2.20).” The cited source instead has γ₅ = iγ₀γ₁γ₂γ₃ = −iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³. This was checked against the PDF's actual subscript/superscript positions; Eq. (10.14) independently gives i^(r+1)γ⁰…γ^(2r−1), hence −iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³ at r=2. See https://arxiv.org/pdf/0802.0634, printed pp. 7 and 80. The item's +1 species therefore has the opposite source chirality, but it retains the source's positive-chirality polynomial and determinant sign. The source-backed identification needs correction or an explicit sign conversion. Conjugate-pair cancellation itself is insensitive to this overall sign.

The Alvarez source locator describes “a local Bardeen–Zumino counterterm” changing “the consistent/covariant representative while preserving the underlying local anomaly data.” This conflates a current correction with an action-counterterm coboundary in the stated consistent BRST quotient. Alvarez §2.4, printed pp. 36–38, explicitly says the covariant anomaly fails the consistency conditions and constructs J_cov = J+Q, Eq. (2.135); it cannot generally be another cocycle representative of the same H^{1,4}(s|d_H) class. See https://members.ift.uam-csic.es/ealvarez/anomalies.ea.pdf. The lemma's conditional quotient argument is sound, but this source annotation is misleading. Similar consistent/covariant wording occurs in def-aqft-thooft-anomaly's Alvarez locator.

alerts.finding: The Definition states γ₅ = iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³ and claims it “matches ... Bilal's mostly-plus positive-chirality convention in Eq. (2.20).” Bilal actually uses the negative of this operator: Eq. (2.20) has i times the four lower-index matrices, and Eq. (10.14) gives −i times the four upper-index matrices in four dimensions. Check https://arxiv.org/pdf/0802.0634, printed pp. 7 and 80. This repeats the batch-41 supplier's source-convention mismatch and affects the signed one-species threshold coefficient.

The Statement uses “γ₅ = iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³” while adopting Bilal's positive-chirality anomaly formula without a chirality sign conversion, then obtains A_H = +∫αG∧G/(24π²) and Γ_WZ = −∫θG∧G/(24π²). Bilal's positive-chirality operator is −iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³, by Eqs. (2.20) and (10.14), https://arxiv.org/pdf/0802.0634. With the other displayed source conventions fixed, the selected eigenspace has opposite source chirality and requires the opposite one-species anomaly sign. The algebra is conditional on the adopted formula, but its claimed source-derived sign is unsupported as written.
